x="672.5" y="450" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="WYEu7sQJ3uWIFPyFZ-jE-28" parent="1" style="shape=cylinder3;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;boundedLbl=1;backgroundOutline=1;size=15;" value="- Signed Qwen3-0.6B model" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="190" width="150" x="350" y="930" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="WYEu7sQJ3uWIFPyFZ-jE-29" parent="1" style="text;html=1;whiteSpace=wrap;strokeColor=none;fillColor=none;align=center;verticalAlign=middle;rounded=0;" value="Cloudflare R2 Storage" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="60" width="100" x="380" y="870" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="WYEu7sQJ3uWIFPyFZ-jE-31" parent="1" style="whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;aspect=fixed;" value="Groq API Whisper" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="80" width="80" x="555" y="960" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="WYEu7sQJ3uWIFPyFZ-jE-40" parent="1" style="rounded=0;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;align=left;" value="<div><u>Why Supabase backend vs traditional custom backend?</u></div><div>Supabase provides Postgres + pgvector, Auth, Row Level Security, Storage, RPCs, and Edge Functions in one managed platform. Much easier to build within this environment than manage a separate Express/FastAPI server and its infrastructure.<u></u></div><div><br></div><u>Why Cloudflare R2 Bucket vs Supabase Storage Bucket?</u><div><div style="">Qwen3-0.6B is approx. ~460MB, Supabase storage = 50mb limit for free version, Cloudflare allows more free storage w/ no egress fees</div><div style=""><br></div><div style=""><div><u>Why profile table in database and user table in Supabase Auth?</u> Supabase Auth stores authentication identity and credentials securely, profiles table stores application-specific user data needed to query and manage.</div><div><br></div><div><u>Why AES-256-GCM encryption?&nbsp;</u></div><div style="line-height: 140%;">needed fast client side auth encryption in one operation, also need cipher text tampering detection (provided with AES-256-GCM).</div><div><br></div><div><u>Why passphrase → KEK → unwrap MEK?</u>&nbsp;</div><div>Deriving a KEK from the user's passphrase lets app securely unwrap a randomly generated MEK without storing the passphrase or plaintext MEK anywhere but users local device</div><div><br></div><div><u>Why semantic vector storing for entries &amp; why chunking?</u></div><div>Semantic vector storage allows for cheap RAG retrieval for search, and chunking to obtain more accurate retrieval and capture different contexts in each journal.</div><div><br></div><div><u>Why Qwen3 0.6B?&nbsp;</u></div><div>Qwen3 0.6B is small enough to run locally with acceptable memory, download size, and latency while still being capable enough for MNEMO's lightweight reranking and journal-related inference.</div><div><br></div><div><u>Why Groq API + Whisper?&nbsp;</u></div><div>Groq provides free + ample hosted Whisper inference, letting MNEMO offer accurate speech-to-text without requiring users' devices to run a large transcription model locally. Tradeoff for privacy hence private storage bucket, however temporary data is being outsourced to cloud platform at user's own discretion</div></div></div>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="605" width="380" x="-1180" y="285" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="WYEu7sQJ3uWIFPyFZ-jE-42" parent="1" style="text;html=1;whiteSpace=wrap;strokeColor=none;fillColor=none;align=center;verticalAlign=middle;rounded=0;" value="Design Choices" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="30" width="150" x="-1080" y="250" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="WYEu7sQJ3uWIFPyFZ-jE-43" parent="1" style="rounded=0;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;align=left;" value="Chunking Entries:<div>- perserves different contexts that can appear in one journal</div><div><br></div><div>Sematic scoring for chunks:</div><div>- gives context numerical scoring for later RAG retrieval and partial encryption of text</div><div><br></div><div>Sematic scoring for search input:</div><div>- matches serach input with semantic vector to match agains t vector DB to return relevant chunks</div><div><br></div><div>RAG retrival pipeline:</div><div>- match input vector against vector DB</div><div>- return top K chunk vectors</div><div>- Decrypt chunks</div><div>- run local keyword matching&nbsp;</div><div>- Fuse rankings with RRF</div><div>- Map winning chunks back to origianl journal entries</div><div><br></div>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="360" width="270" x="-785" y="315" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="WYEu7sQJ3uWIFPyFZ-jE-44" parent="1" style="text;html=1;whiteSpace=wrap;strokeColor=none;fillColor=none;align=center;verticalAlign=middle;rounded=0;" value="RAG Retrival Pipeline" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="30" width="150" x="-720" y="285" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="WYEu7sQJ3uWIFPyFZ-jE-45" parent="1" style="text;html=1;whiteSpace=wrap;strokeColor=none;fillColor=none;align=center;verticalAlign=middle;rounded=0;" value="LLM Optimization" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="30" width="150" x="-440" y="280" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="WYEu7sQJ3uWIFPyFZ-jE-46" parent="1" style="rounded=0;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;align=left;" value="Model choice (Qwen3-0.6b):<div>- smaller model from larger Gemma models</div><div>- cuts model size and local compute</div><div><br></div><div>Stored pre-quantized model GGUF in Cloudflare R2 Storage:</div><div>- quantized model approximates model weights</div><div>- less RAM needed on user device</div><div>- faster inference</div><div><br></div><div>WebGPU:</div><div>- offloads matrix calculation to WebGPU if available for faster parallel calculations over CPU</div><div><br></div><div>WASM:</div><div>- allows complied low-level code to run in browser with user cpu</div><div>- inference code compiled to WASM runs more efficiently on users CPU, faster token generation</div><div><br></div><div>KV Caching:</div><div>- cache journal context during preproccessing</div><div>- prevents repeat processing for context to answer user input</div><div><br></div>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="405" width="270" x="-500" y="310" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> </root> </mxGraphModel> </diagram> </mxfile>

div.u: Why Supabase backend vs traditional custom backend?

div.div: Supabase provides Postgres + pgvector, Auth, Row Level Security, Storage, RPCs, and Edge Functions in one managed platform. Much easier to build within this environment than manage a separate Express/FastAPI server and its infrastructure.
div.u: Why Cloudflare R2 Bucket vs Supabase Storage Bucket?

div.div: Qwen3-0.6B is approx. ~460MB, Supabase storage = 50mb limit for free version, Cloudflare allows more free storage w/ no egress fees

Why profile table in database and user table in Supabase Auth? Supabase Auth stores authentication identity and credentials securely, profiles table stores application-specific user data needed to query and manage.

div.style: line-height: 140%;

div.div: needed fast client side auth encryption in one operation, also need cipher text tampering detection (provided with AES-256-GCM).
Deriving a KEK from the user's passphrase lets app securely unwrap a randomly generated MEK without storing the passphrase or plaintext MEK anywhere but users local device

div.u: Why semantic vector storing for entries & why chunking?

div.div: Semantic vector storage allows for cheap RAG retrieval for search, and chunking to obtain more accurate retrieval and capture different contexts in each journal.
Qwen3 0.6B is small enough to run locally with acceptable memory, download size, and latency while still being capable enough for MNEMO's lightweight reranking and journal-related inference.

Groq provides free + ample hosted Whisper inference, letting MNEMO offer accurate speech-to-text without requiring users' devices to run a large transcription model locally. Tradeoff for privacy hence private storage bucket, however temporary data is being outsourced to cloud platform at user's own discretion

div.div:
Chunking Entries:
- perserves different contexts that can appear in one journal
Sematic scoring for chunks:
- gives context numerical scoring for later RAG retrieval and partial encryption of text
Sematic scoring for search input:
- matches serach input with semantic vector to match agains t vector DB to return relevant chunks
RAG retrival pipeline:
- match input vector against vector DB
- return top K chunk vectors
- Decrypt chunks
- run local keyword matching
- Fuse rankings with RRF
- Map winning chunks back to origianl journal entries

div.div:
Model choice (Qwen3-0.6b):
- smaller model from larger Gemma models
- cuts model size and local compute
Stored pre-quantized model GGUF in Cloudflare R2 Storage:
- quantized model approximates model weights
- less RAM needed on user device
- faster inference
WebGPU:
- offloads matrix calculation to WebGPU if available for faster parallel calculations over CPU
WASM:
- allows complied low-level code to run in browser with user cpu
- inference code compiled to WASM runs more efficiently on users CPU, faster token generation
KV Caching:
- cache journal context during preproccessing
- prevents repeat processing for context to answer user input
